sb_prompt: FIND OUT WHAT KIND OF PETS THE OTHER CALLER HAS.
raw_output:
ParticipantA: Hey, yeah, hi.
ParticipantB: Oh, hello there.
ParticipantA: How are you doing today?
ParticipantB: Pretty good, I guess. Just a slow day at the bank.
ParticipantB: I was wondering what kind of pets you have? Do you have any?
ParticipantA: Oh, yeah, I do. Two dogs.
ParticipantA: Golden Retriever mix and a little Chihuahua.
ParticipantB: Oh, nice. I love dogs.
ParticipantB: I don't have any right now, though.
ParticipantA: That's too bad. Someone needs to pet something.
ParticipantB: Yeah, well, it's kind of complicated.
ParticipantA: Complicated how?
ParticipantB: Well, my sister-in-law, she's got three cats and two dogs.
ParticipantA: Really? That's a lot of animals.
ParticipantB: Yeah, and it's just... it's a mess.
ParticipantB: She spends half her paycheck on vet bills and food.
ParticipantB: And honestly, she doesn't even know them well enough to call them names.
ParticipantA: Oh, wow. That sounds tough.
ParticipantA: I never thought about it that way. I thought people just got pets because they love them.
ParticipantB: Well, that's the thing. People think they want them, but then the cost hits.
ParticipantB: Or they get lonely and buy something to fill the silence.
ParticipantA: Hmm. I have a friend who did that.
ParticipantA: Bought a dog after his divorce.
ParticipantB: Yeah, exactly. Turned out the dog had behavioral issues.
ParticipantB: They couldn't handle it. Had to give it up.
ParticipantA: Oh, that's sad.
ParticipantA: I tried to help her fix it, but it just got worse.
ParticipantA: Now the dog is with a shelter and my friend is crying.
ParticipantB: That's rough. Sometimes I wonder if we're doing it right.
ParticipantB: I know a guy who was going to get a horse.
ParticipantB: Said he wanted to ride, but then he realized he couldn't afford the tack or the farrier.
ParticipantA: Yeah, that makes sense. It's a big commitment.
ParticipantA: I tell my clients all the time, "Don't buy a house you can't afford."
ParticipantB: Oh, really? You're a realtor?
ParticipantA: Yeah, I am.
ParticipantB: Oh, okay. That explains it.
ParticipantB: I'm a teller, so I see a lot of people trying to save for that first one.
ParticipantB: But then they buy the pet and it becomes a financial burden.
ParticipantA: Yeah, exactly.
ParticipantA: I had a client, older guy, really nice.
ParticipantA: He wanted a big dog to run around in the yard.
ParticipantB: Yeah?
ParticipantA: Turns out he was retired and had a stiff neck.
ParticipantB: Oh no.
ParticipantA: He couldn't walk it. Couldn't lift it.
ParticipantA: Had to surrender the dog to a shelter.
ParticipantB: That must have been hard for him.
ParticipantA: Yeah, he was devastated.
ParticipantA: Said he felt like he lied to the animal.
ParticipantB: That's a heavy price to pay.
ParticipantB: I guess I wouldn't do it if I knew it was going to end up like that.
ParticipantA: Me neither.
ParticipantA: It's better to be honest with yourself before you bring one home.
ParticipantB: True.
ParticipantB: I think I'll stick to volunteering at the shelter for now.
ParticipantA: Good idea. You can help without adding to the burden.
ParticipantB: Yeah, that feels better.
ParticipantA: And no vet bills for you.
ParticipantB: Exactly.
ParticipantA: Well, I'm glad we talked about it.
ParticipantB: Me too. Thanks for listening.
ParticipantA: No problem. Take care.
ParticipantB: Bye.
